candidates: When adding a new parameter or property to a function in a JavaScript (non-TypeScript) file, add at minimum a JSDoc comment documenting the new addition—even if the surrounding code has no existing documentation. For functions that accept plain objects, use a `@typedef` to describe the object shape (including the new field) and a `@param` tag on the function itself. Full typing of pre-existing fields is not required; documenting only the new addition is acceptable.

When using an empirically derived or visually tuned numeric constant that is non-round or otherwise surprising (e.g. `7.9`, `15.5` for SVG marker positioning), add an inline comment explaining that the value is intentional and how it was arrived at, so reviewers can distinguish deliberate fine-tuning from a typo.
